author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: The Author Works page state is duplicated between the titlar and mer routes.
findings.consequence: Future changes to Author Works route identity, async cache keys, stale-response rejection, SSR status mapping, or quick-search publication must be kept in sync across two route files, so one variant can regress independently of the other.
findings.evidence: The owned identity line `titlar:${authorId.value}` begins the same route-state pattern used by `app/pages/författare/[author]/mer.vue`: both files define the same authorId extraction, `author-works:${currentIdentity.value}` async key, `/authors/{author_id}/works` request, response identity guard, two accepted-state watchers, SSR status mapping, works computed, and quick-search publisher. The differences are limited to variant identity and display copy.
findings.recommendation: Extract the shared behavior into a small composable such as `useAuthorWorksPage({ variant, descriptionLabel })` that returns `authorId`, `accepted`, `works`, and `description`; keep each route responsible only for variant-specific labels and template text.
